At Halter, we know how much farmers care - for their animals and their pasture. But the tools they rely on haven’t kept up, and we’re on a mission to change that. Halter helps farmers make smarter decisions - fast. We reckon good pasture management is the key to more productive and sustainable farms. More grass. Healthier soil. Happier animals. And more time back for the people doing the work.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for Lead Engineers who perform at the top of the craft. You'll take on the hardest problems, make the calls that matter on the gnarliest design questions, and ship work that the rest of the team learns from. Engineers around you get better because they're working alongside you. We don't mind whether your strengths sit on the frontend, backend, full stack, or on the platform side that gives every other engineer leverage. What matters is that you ship robust, thoughtful work at a level few others can match, and use AI tools well.




THE KIND OF PROBLEMS OUR TEAMS SOLVE

Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. Our engineering teams own different slices of that system, but the problems all rhyme:

 - Turning thousands of collars and billions of sensor events into a single, calm decision in a farmer's hand.

 - Modelling the physical world (animals, pasture, terrain) accurately enough to act on in real time.

 - Building mobile and web experiences that hold up at 5am whilst out in a paddock in the rain.

 - Designing platforms and pipelines that scale with our incredible pace of growth without the seams showing.

 - Engineering against constrained hardware, flaky rural connectivity, and the messiness of the physical world, and shipping with pace despite it.

Every team here ships software that has to work in a paddock, not just a browser tab.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Take on the hardest problems and ship the work that proves them out.

 - Make the architectural calls that matter, then back them up by writing the code.

 - Set the standard for thoughtful engineering: clean, observable, easy-to-evolve code and systems.

 - Support and mentor other engineers through design conversations, code reviews, and generous context sharing.

 - Help set the pace and quality bar for engineering at Halter.

 - Help evolve our testing strategies, CI/CD workflows, and infrastructure patterns.

 - Own the reliability and performance of your domain, especially when things get tricky. Every team owns its services end-to-end, with an on-call rotation.

 - Get out on farm. Deep domain knowledge matters, and you'll be expected to develop it.
   
    


YOU'LL BE GREAT IF YOU:

 - Have spent years shipping complex systems in production and have the experience (and scars) to show for it.

 - Stay calm under pressure, have a low ego, and can rally a team through tough or complex work.

 - Think like a product engineer: you care about the customer experience, not just clean code.

 - Know how to use AI tools well to lift team output and focus on the harder stuff.

 - Have grown other engineers by working alongside them, not by managing them.

 - Are comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where adaptability beats perfection.

 - Have worked in cloud environments. AWS is a bonus.

 - A degree in software engineering (or equivalent) is nice to have, but not essential.
   
    


DEPENDING ON WHERE YOU SIT ON THE STACK, SOME OF THESE WILL LAND HARDER THAN OTHERS:

 - Frontend / Mobile: strong UX intuition, modern frontend frameworks (React, React Native a bonus), an eye for performance and polish on real devices.
   
   Backend: building and scaling REST APIs, distributed systems, and event-driven services. Comfort with both relational and non-relational databases. Node.js, Kotlin, Go, or systems that integrate with hardware/IoT a bonus.
   
   Full stack: all of the above, end to end, across web, mobile, and the services that power them.
   
   Platform: you love building tooling that makes the whole company move faster, including the AI tooling that's reshaping how engineers work. Strong AWS and Terraform at scale, with experience across CI/CD, observability, and on-call tooling.
   
    


OUR BENEFITS

 - Delicious snacks

 - Deep electronics engineering experience, with hands-on experience debugging complex hardware.

 - Experience with diagnosing field failures and understanding the relationships between in-field events and product failures

 - Excellent communication skills and the ability to translate technical findings into clear feedback for cross-functional teams.

 - A natural inclination to share knowledge, to educate and mentor

 - A deep curiosity and principled approach to finding root causes with clear evidence.

 - Strong sense of ownership and a bias for action - you’re not afraid to roll up your sleeves and get stuck into wider challenges when required.

We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!

Please also feel free to check out the careers page https://www.halterhq.com/careers for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations.

We’re looking for a highly capable and first-principled individual to join our Failure Analysis team and debug failed hardware to root cause, both from the field and lab testing. Halter collars aren’t serviced, aren’t repairable and need to last 6-10 years, anywhere across the globe. To achieve this, we need to know about every failure in the field and how to eliminate it.

You’ll be responsible for debugging and diagnosing failed hardware, including collars and tower components, to deeply understand the root cause. Halter products are complex, highly integrated electromechanical devices, and debugging and root-causing the many different failure modes that occur requires an inquisitive mindset and methodical approach. This is both a technical and operational role where you will be central to closing the feedback loop between our lab & field performance and our engineering teams, ensuring that each failure is investigated, understood, and used to improve product reliability.

 - Electronics engineering experience, with hands-on experience debugging hardware.

 - Experience with diagnosing field failures and understanding the relationships between in-field events and product failures

 - Excellent communication skills to share your technical findings with others

 - A deep curiosity and first-principles approach to finding root causes with clear evidence.

As a South American Launch Specialist, you'll be one of the first people on the ground establishing Halter's presence across the region — and you'll own what it means to bring Halter to producers in Argentina, Uruguay, and Brazil for the first time.

You'll lead the rollout of Halter on new operations end-to-end: training cattle and operators, solving problems in the field, and supporting producers as they get started. This role is partially field-based. Expect roughly a 70/30 split toward time on the ground, with regular travel across Argentina, Uruguay, and Brazil. You'll be with customers where they run their cattle, and the quality of what you build depends on you being there and understanding their operations deeply..

It's practical, hands-on, and highly ownership-driven. Every operation is different, and you'll tailor each deployment to help producers build confidence with Halter.  - Work directly with producers to bring Halter into their operation and support day-to-day use

 - Lead training that fits the operation: practical, straightforward, and useful

 - Act as the main point of contact during deployment, giving customers a clear, reliable owner

 - Partner closely with Sales, Support, Product, and Operations to keep deployments coordinated across borders

 - Keep deployments on track by managing timelines, aligning resources, and clearing blockers

 - Solve problems quickly and adapt plans as conditions change — language, terrain, and infrastructure will all vary

 - Spot patterns in the field and feed them directly to Product to shape how Halter works for the region

 - Set customers up with the confidence and foundation needed for long-term success with Halter

 - Whatever else it takes: This is an early-stage market entry. You’ll do what needs doing to make Halter succeed in South America.

 - Experience working with customers: whether onboarding, supporting, deploying, or managing complex rollouts

 - Genuine comfort with travel and field work

 - Fluency in Spanish and English, Portuguese is a bonus.

 - Confidence operating independently and keeping priorities organized

 - The ability to coordinate moving pieces and keep things progressing without constant oversight

 - A practical, solutions-focused mindset when challenges come up

 - Comfort working cross-functionally: pulling in the right people and keeping everyone aligned

 - Clear, straightforward communication

 - Good judgment and the ability to adapt when plans change

 - A genuine care for the people we serve and the quality of the work

 - Agriculture or cattle ranching experience, especially with extensive grazing systems

English proficiency is a requirement for this role. ABOUT THE ROLE

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the Southern region of Arkansas. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halt

We’re looking for a Product Manager to join our Virtual Fencing team.

Virtual Fencing is the heart of Halter. It’s how thousands of farmers across the world manage their animals. Halter is often farmers #1 app on their phone and we have the privilege of building the experience that farmers use to look after their animals.

This role is all about deeply understanding what our farmers need from our product and taking those insights and converting them into beautiful elegant features that help our farmers run their farm. This role sits right at the intersection of technology and farming. You will become an expert in virtual fencing; developing a deep understanding of how the technology works and how farmers and ranchers use it in practice. ABOUT THE ROLE

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US. 

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. 

In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers. Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups. 



This role covers the South West region of Minnesota. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers. 

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups. 

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. ABOUT THE ROLE

As Senior Manager, Commercial Strategy, you'll own the future growth path for Halter. You'll set the commercial strategy that accelerates adoption, unlocks new markets, and helps us win before competitors even see us coming — and you'll roll up your sleeves to make it happen.

Reporting to the VP Commercial Strategy, this is a senior leadership role and a deeply hands-on one. You'll be a key partner to the VP and the wider commercial leadership group, helping shape where Halter plays and how we win — and then doing the work to get there. You'll build and lead a small, high-calibre team over time, but you'll lead from the front: in the model, in the field, and in the detail. This is a player-coach role, not a hands-off one.

You'll move fluidly between the strategy and the paddock — one moment framing a market-entry thesis, the next on the ground with farmers and ranchers pressure-testing it in reality, the next going deep with finance on our CAC model.

This is a rare opportunity to shape one of the most transformative companies in agriculture, lead our most important commercial decisions, and leave your fingerprints on the trajectory of the entire company.



What your day could look like

 - Continuously evolve Halter's commercial strategy - where we play, how we win, and where we place our biggest bets across markets, channels, and segments. You set the commercial strategy and the priorities; then lead your team and partners to execute against them.

 - Be the go-to strategic partner to the VP Commercial on Halter's most consequential commercial decisions.

 - Help to mentor a small, high-performing Commercial Strategy team - while staying hands-on in the work yourself.

 - Do the work - build the models, write the narratives, and run the analysis yourself, not just direct others to.

 - Lead the most complex, cross-functional bets across GTM, Product, and Ops - from new-market entry to new channels and partnerships.

 - Own market intelligence and competitive strategy - anticipating shifts, farmer needs, and macro trends to keep Halter several moves ahead.

 - Set the long-term frameworks for how Halter monetises new capabilities and enters new markets, and hold the org accountable to them.

 - Define and stand up Halter's strategic partnership strategy - identifying, structuring, and scaling the partnership models that unlock new distribution, data, and revenue.

 - Build the financial backbone for big decisions: Opportunity sizing, scenario analysis, and the structures that drive crisp decision-making.

 - Turn complex, ambiguous problems into clear narratives and decisions for leaders and frontline teams.

 - Drive adoption end-to-end - ensuring strategies don't just get approved, but get executed, measured, and improved across the business.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You're a seasoned commercial strategist who builds real-world engines, not just frameworks, playbooks, and pitch decks.

 - You can crack the messiest, highest-stakes problems, build the model that reveals the answer, and then mobilise the organisation to move.

 - You're deeply commercial. You understand the levers - growth, pricing, unit economics, partnerships, market entry - and you know how and when to pull them.

 - You're a doer first. You'd rather build the model and ship the v1 yourself than delegate it - and your team learns by watching you set the standard.

 - You can build and coach a small team as the function grows, while staying a strong individual contributor in your own right.

 - You earn the trust of senior leaders quickly and can influence decisions without needing positional authority - but you're equally happy in the weeds doing the work.

 - Ambiguity doesn't scare you; you run toward it. You think clearly, communicate crisply, and turn complex ideas into simple, actionable stories people rally behind.

 - You've got range and altitude. One day you're framing a multi-year market thesis; the next you're in the spreadsheet or unblocking sales so the strategy actually lands.

 - You're a champion of cross-functional collaboration - across Sales, Marketing, Finance, Product, and Ops - and you make everyone around you sharper.



YOU'LL CRUSH THIS GIG I

You'll partner with local leaders and the global P&P team to stand up the core people infrastructure for a new market — then keep raising the bar as the team scales.

 - Coaching managers through feedback, performance conversations, development, and early employee relations matters

 - Owning onboarding quality so new starters understand the mission, operating model, and cultural bar from day one

 - Running people logistics — systems, documentation, compliance, and employee information

 - Supporting market-entry operations: office setup, field-team logistics, local vendor coordination, fleet and vehicle processes

 - Staying close to the ground and feeding signal back to People, Talent, Commercial, and leadership

 - Are willing to challenge leaders when the standard is slipping

 - Want to help shape the culture of a new market from day one

This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the Alberta region in Canada.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of Canadian ranchers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the North West region of Saskatchewan. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the cust

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're changing the way the world farms — and with that comes a responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. We're looking for an experienced Electronics Engineer to join our Failure Analysis team and debug failed electronics down to root cause, from both the field and lab testing.

Halter collars aren't serviced, aren't repairable, and need to last 6–10 years, anywhere across the globe. Our products are complex, highly integrated electromechanical devices packed with ultra-low power circuitry, RF, solar and battery systems, high-voltage pulse circuits, and dense multi-layer PCBs. To make them last, we need to understand every electronic failure mode in the field and know exactly how to eliminate it.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Personally own the highest-impact and most ambiguous electronic failure modes, driving them to a clear, evidence-based root cause. This is a hands-on role; you'll be very close to the electronics.

 - Debug and diagnose failed electronics at the sub-system and component level: power generation and conversion, ultra-low power circuits, RF and antenna, battery systems, high-voltage pulse circuits, and the MCUs, SoCs, sensors and interfaces around them.

 - Use the full bench of EE diagnostic tools (oscilloscopes, DMM, network analyzers, signal generators, LCR meters, current clamps, HV meters, thermal imaging, microscopy and X-ray where relevant) to isolate faults.

 - Understand the relationships between in-field events and electronic failures, connecting field data and returns to physical failure signatures on the hardware.

 - Develop and improve the processes, tooling and ways of working that increase diagnostic accuracy and reduce no-fault-founds.

 - Work closely with hardware, firmware, production and supplier quality teams to investigate failures and drive corrective action into the design.

 - Mentor and guide more junior engineers, expanding their technical knowledge and their approach to failure analysis.

 - Support recruitment for building out a brilliant team, rooted in strong process discipline, technical capability and a tenacious curiosity to figure things out.

This is a deeply technical, hands-on role at the board and component level. You'll diagnose failed collar and tower electronics, isolate faults to the specific component, net, or design decision responsible, and translate that understanding into clear, evidence-based feedback that improves product reliability. You'll be central to closing the loop between field and lab performance and our hardware, firmware, and production teams.

This is a huge opportunity for the right person - you'll have a lasting impact on farmers across the globe.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Solid electronics engineering experience, with hands-on expertise diagnosing field failures and connecting real-world events to product failure modes for complex, highly integrated hardware at the board and component level.

 - A methodical, first-principled approach to root cause analysis, backed by clear evidence rather than assumption.

 - Strong grounding in electronic circuit fundamentals across analog, digital, power and RF; ideally including ultra-low power IoT designs, batteries, solar, DC-DC conversion, high-voltage generation and insulation, and interfaces such as I2C and SPI.

 - Proficiency with EE diagnostic and test equipment, and comfortable reading schematics and PCB layouts to trace faults.

 - Excellent communication skills and the ability to translate technical findings into clear, actionable feedback for cross-functional teams.

 - A natural inclination to share knowledge, educate and mentor.

 - A strong sense of ownership and a bias for action — you're not afraid to roll up your sleeves and get stuck into wider challenges when required.

 - Low ego, highly collaborative, and willing to play for the Front of the Jersey.

 - A BE degree in Electrical/Electronic Engineering or a similar relevant qualification.

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the Northern region of Arizona. Frequent travel is expected as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halte

 - Upskill the team: Train the Customer Experience Support team to recognise and resolve more complex issues themselves, reducing the number of cases that need to be escalated.

 - Measure what matters: Track and report on escalation and customer health metrics, such as open escalations, time to resolution, customers recovered and recurring issues.

 - Be there when it counts: take part in on-call or roster coverage to support incident response, including weather events and farm-wide outages.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our wireless network engineering team - the team that keeps one of the world's largest private IoT networks connected. Over a million devices across New Zealand, Australia, the US and Canada, spanning LoRa, cellular, and satellite direct-to-device, running on remote infrastructure in some of the hardest terrain there is.

This isn't a pure delivery or pure people role. You'll be in the work: shaping the network architecture, weighing in on spectrum strategy and link budgets, reviewing the automation that runs our tower fleet, and helping your team do the best work of their careers. You'll need to hold the technical bar high while creating the space for others to grow.

We're solving connectivity problems that haven't been solved before - keeping livestock connected hundreds of kilometres from the nearest town, where there's often no coverage at all. It's a role that demands absolute ownership: someone who can take a blurry problem, create clarity, and lead a team to nail it.




THE KIND OF PROBLEMS YOUR TEAM SOLVES

Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. The wireless network team owns the connectivity layer everything else depends on:

 - Keeping over a million collars connected across LoRa, cellular, and satellite direct-to-device - in valleys, over ridgelines, and far beyond the edge of conventional coverage.

 - Planning coverage with real RF engineering: link budgets, path loss modelling, antenna selection, and spectrum strategy across multiple regulatory regimes.

 - Running a fleet of thousands of remote towers with zero-touch provisioning, configuration automation, and remote diagnostics - a truck roll to a hill-country site is expensive, so software has to do the work.

 - Squeezing every byte: our devices are power and bandwidth constrained, so protocol efficiency and data optimisation directly shape the product.

 - Making network health visible - turning telemetry from millions of radio links into signals engineers and field teams can act on.

Every team here ships systems that have to work in a paddock, not just a browser tab. As an engineering manager at Halter, you're in the work, not above it: coaching engineers, shaping the technical bets, and staying hands-on.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead a team of wireless network engineers - supporting their growth, giving great feedback, running performance conversations, and helping them focus on what matters.

 - Own the technical direction and delivery of the network: architecture, reliability, and scalability across collar-to-tower-to-cloud connectivity.

 - Stay close to the technical details - spectrum allocation and compliance, LoRa and cellular behaviour, tower infrastructure, fleet configuration automation, and the software tooling that ties it together - and bring a strong point of view.

 - Own network reliability outcomes: uptime, incident response, and the on-call practices that keep a 24/7 physical network healthy without burning the team out.

 - Drive tower deployment and coverage strategy as we scale into new regions - site selection, RF planning, and delivery of critical infrastructure.

 - Hire and grow the team. Wireless network engineering is a rare skill mix, and you'll be building a world-class bench of it.

 - Work closely with firmware, backend, hardware, and field operations to shape what we build, not just how. You'll be in the room when requirements are fuzzy and you'll help make them clear.

 - Back engineering-led initiatives and look for opportunities to use AI tools to accelerate development or unlock entirely new ways of working.

 - Get out on farm. Deep domain knowledge matters and you'll be expected to develop it.

 - Contribute to the broader engineering culture and practices that make Halter a great place to build.


YOU'LL BE GREAT IF YOU

You’ll work closely with hiring managers to understand their team needs, anticipate upcoming roles, and manage end-to-end recruitment processes that ensure we bring in exceptional people who align with our mission and values.

Reporting to the Talent Lead, you’ll focus on executing recruitment strategies, managing candidate pipelines, and delivering an outstanding candidate experience that reflects the calibre of our product and culture.  - Build scalable recruitment practices and foundations, designing processes, tools, and ways of working that can flex across regions, functions, and increasing hiring volumes.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a motivated, hands-on Field Ops Specialist to join our team as one of our first hardware technicians on the ground in Australia. What is the hardware? The collars and towers that are what makes us Halter. This is a rare opportunity to be part of something genuinely new.

You’ll be responsible for building an efficient operational system from the ground up, getting out onto farms, and making sure our hardware infrastructure runs without a hitch. One moment you’re diagnosing a technical issue in the field, the next you’re delivering collars to a new producer. You’ll be the go-to person on the ground, the kind of person who takes ownership and gets things done.

You’ll work closely with dedicated teams in Australia, and at Halter’s Auckland HQ. You’ll play a key role in making sure our pioneering producers in the region get an unmatched experience from day one.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Infrastructure maintenance: Oversee the upkeep and repair of Halter’s on-farm infrastructure to keep operations running smoothly.

 - Hardware diagnosis: Diagnose issues with our hardware and feed that information back to the right team quickly.

 - Deployment support: Get out onto farms to help deploy Halter. Troubleshoot issues, support installations, and make sure things go well.

 - Field insights: Feed your learnings back clearly to our product and engineering teams, so we’re always building what matters most for Australian cattle producers.

 - On-call: Be part of our global on-call roster to support tower-related incidents and proactively find solutions in a timely manner.

 - Data analysis: Collect, interpret, and analyse data from our hardware to optimise processes and improve operational efficiency. Spot issues before they become problems.

 - Maintenance system: Help build and manage a maintenance system tailored to the Australian market.

 - Collaboration: Work closely across Halter’s teams to stay aligned and drive strong customer outcomes.

 - Travel: With producers spread across Australia, you’ll be on the road regularly. Expect 3 to 4 days a week and some nights away from home.

 - Whatever else it takes: You’ll do what needs doing to make Halter continue to succeed in Australia.

 - Hands-on experience: Practical experience with tools, electrical work, construction, networking, or equipment fitting is a must.

 - Go-getter attitude: You’re proactive, you take ownership, and you’re not afraid to figure things out on the go.

 - Strong communicator: You can translate what you’re seeing in the field into clear, actionable feedback for a remote product and engineering team.

 - Time management: You manage your own time well and get tasks done on schedule without someone looking over your shoulder.

 - Team player: You work well with people across different locations and time zones.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity: This is early-stage market entry. Things will be imperfect. You’ll thrive on that rather than be frustrated by it.

 - Willingness to travel: You’re up for regular and sometimes spontaneous travel across the region.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

The Role

Halter builds hardware that works in some of the most demanding environments on earth. The quality of what we ship matters enormously, to the farmers who depend on it every day and to the mission we're on. As we scale into multiple products and higher volumes, we need someone to own quality across the full supply chain and build it into a genuine competitive advantage.

The Director of Supply Chain Quality owns Halter's end-to-end quality function, based at our Auckland HQ. You'll lead two teams: a Supplier Quality team that owns quality at our component suppliers from pre-selection auditing through to ongoing part approval, and a Contract Manufacturing Quality team that owns incoming, in-process, and outgoing quality at our contract manufacturers. Together they form a quality system with clear accountability and no gaps.

A critical part of this role is owning Halter's quality assurance specifications, developed and maintained in collaboration with the Supplier Quality team, the Contract Manufacturing Quality team, and the hardware design team. These specs are the backbone of the quality system. Getting them right and keeping them current is what makes everything else work.

You'll set the quality strategy, develop your team leaders and their teams, own the quality framework across the supply chain, and be the escalation point when quality issues arise at the boundary between supplier and CM. You'll work closely with hardware engineering, operations, and sourcing to ensure quality is designed in and not just inspected for.

This is not a documentation role. The best quality leaders get into the detail. They visit suppliers, they walk the production line, they dig into the data behind a failure mode, and they develop a sharp instinct for what actually drives quality outcomes versus what just adds paperwork. We want someone who is technically curious, comfortable getting their hands dirty, and able to distinguish between a process that genuinely improves quality and one that exists to say it exists.

You'll be measured on product quality, supplier and CM quality performance, and your ability to build a quality function that scales with Halter's growth.


What You'll Do

Leadership and Team Development

 - Lead and develop the Supplier Quality and Contract Manufacturing Quality teams, setting clear direction, holding a high bar, and developing strong people in both functions.

 - Build the culture of the quality function: rigorous, fast-moving, low bureaucracy, and deeply connected to the engineering and operations teams.

 - Set clear accountability between the two teams and own the interface between them, ensuring the handoff between supplier OQC and CM IQC is well-governed and issues at the boundary are resolved quickly.

Quality Assurance Specifications

 - Own the development and ongoing maintenance of Halter's quality assurance specifications, working across the Supplier Quality team, the Contract Manufacturing Quality team, and the hardware design team to ensure specs reflect current design intent and are correctly implemented across the supply chain.

 - Ensure QA specs are the single source of truth for what quality standards are required at suppliers and at our CMs, and that they are kept current as products evolve.

 - Define the governance model for how QA specs are reviewed, approved, and updated, and ensure all three teams are aligned on the process.

Quality Strategy and Systems

 - Own Halter's quality management system across the supply chain, ensuring it is fit for purpose, consistently applied, and evolves as the business scales.

 - Build the quality metrics and reporting that give leadership a clear and honest picture of quality performance across suppliers and contract manufacturers.

 - Lead root cause analysis and corrective action on significant quality escapes, ensuring lessons are captured and systemic issues are fixed rather than managed.

 - Collaborate with the Operations Delivery Lead and Head of Supply Chain Strategy to ensure quality risks are visible early in NPI programmes and sustaining activities.


What You Bring

 - Significant experience leading quality functions in a hardware or electronics manufacturing environme

Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. Our engineering teams own different slices of that system, but the problems all rhyme:

 - Turning thousands of collars and billions of sensor events into a single, calm decision in a farmer's hand.

 - Modelling the physical world (animals, pasture, terrain) accurately enough to act on in real time.

 - Building mobile and web experiences that hold up at 5am whilst out in a paddock in the rain.

 - Designing platforms and pipelines that scale with our incredible pace of growth without the seams showing.

 - Engineering against constrained hardware, flaky rural connectivity, and the messiness of the physical world, and shipping with pace despite it.

Every team here ships software that has to work in a paddock, not just a browser tab.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Take on the hardest problems and ship the work that proves them out.

 - Make the architectural calls that matter, then back them up by writing the code.

 - Set the standard for thoughtful engineering: clean, observable, easy-to-evolve code and systems.

 - Support and mentor other engineers through design conversations, code reviews, and generous context sharing.

 - Help set the pace and quality bar for engineering at Halter.

 - Help evolve our testing strategies, CI/CD workflows, and infrastructure patterns.

 - Own the reliability and performance of your domain, especially when things get tricky. Every team owns its services end-to-end, with an on-call rotation.

 - Get out on farm. Deep domain knowledge matters, and you'll be expected to develop it.
   
    


YOU'LL BE GREAT IF YOU:

 - Have spent years shipping complex systems in production and have the experience (and scars) to show for it.

 - Stay calm under pressure, have a low ego, and can rally a team through tough or complex work.

 - Think like a product engineer: you care about the customer experience, not just clean code.

 - Know how to use AI tools well to lift team output and focus on the harder stuff.

 - Have grown other engineers by working alongside them, not by managing them.

 - Are comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where adaptability beats perfection.

 - Have worked in cloud environments. AWS is a bonus.

 - A degree in software engineering (or equivalent) is nice to have, but not essential.
   
    


DEPENDING ON WHERE YOU SIT ON THE STACK, SOME OF THESE WILL LAND HARDER THAN OTHERS:

 - Frontend / Mobile: strong UX intuition, modern frontend frameworks (React, React Native a bonus), an eye for performance and polish on real devices.
   
   Backend: building and scaling REST APIs, distributed systems, and event-driven services. Comfort with both relational and non-relational databases. Node.js, Kotlin, Go, or systems that integrate with hardware/IoT a bonus.
   
   Full stack: all of the above, end to end, across web, mobile, and the services that power them.
   
   Platform: you love building tooling that makes the whole company move faster, including the AI tooling that's reshaping how engineers work. Strong AWS and Terraform at scale, with experience across CI/CD, observability, and on-call tooling.
   
    


OUR BENEFITS

ABOUT THE ROLE

Halter is scaling global production of connected livestock wearables while still making meaningful product and manufacturing changes. Our engineering decisions are well owned. We now need a dedicated owner for the BOMs, change records and planning visibility those decisions depend on.

You'll keep product, process, supplier and validation records complete, traceable and current. Engineering, Quality, Production, Supply Chain, suppliers and contract manufacturers will build from one reliable source of truth, including a forward view of upcoming BOM changes and their build impact.

"Manager" here means ownership of systems, records and coordination. It is not people management initially, and it is not approval authority over engineering changes.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Run engineering change control end to end in Arena: ECO/ECN records, affected items, redlines, effectivity and implementation timing, through to cut-in at our contract manufacturers.

 - Own BOM integrity: part numbers, revisions, lifecycles, HPN/MPN and approved manufacturer lists, with EBOM and MBOM kept aligned with what CMs actually build.

 - Publish a weekly forward BOM plan for Supply Chain covering upcoming changes, validation state, implementation timing, supply risk and build impact.

 - Keep Onshape → Arena and Altium → Arena traceability reliable, and publish released documents to their relevant homes.

 - Administer our Arena deployment: configuration, lifecycles, roles, permissions, supplier access, onboarding, training and data quality.

 - Build and run practical registers for changes in flight, waivers and deviations, supplier-document status, document currency, missing records and overdue items.

 - Co-define release-boundary conventions with Engineering and Quality, then keep them easy to follow and consistently applied.

 - Give decision owners clear status reporting, so they act on facts instead of hunting through systems.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Hands-on experience with BOMs and engineering change in hardware, electronics, medical device or automotive manufacturing. You've raised, routed and implemented ECOs, not only filed them.

 - Administrator-level experience with a PLM system such as Arena, Windchill, Teamcenter or Agile. Arena is a bonus; the discipline matters more than the platform.

 - Fluency with revisions, effectivity, EBOM→MBOM, HPN/MPN, AML/AVL, waivers and deviations, and clear-to-build planning.

 - Experience working with contract manufacturers or suppliers to land BOM changes on the line.

 - Exceptional attention to detail and follow-through. You notice stale revisions, quietly expired waivers, unclear ownership and changes that will hit an upcoming build.

 - Strong written communication, sound judgement, and the persistence to follow up warmly until open items close.

 - Willingness to travel occasionally to suppliers and production sites, for example for supplier onboarding or change cut-ins.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience in a design-controlled or regulated environment, such as ISO 13485 or IATF 16949.

 - Electronics BOM experience, including PCBA revisions and Altium-to-PLM workflows.

 - ERP/MRP integration experience, so BOM changes flow cleanly into planning.


LOCATION AND WORK RIGHTS

This role is based in Auckland, working on site with our Production team. You'll need the existing right to work in New Zealand or be open to relocation and visa sponsorship to Auckland, NZ.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. Our platform is what turns that ambitious engineering into farmer and rancher impact. Every collar on every cow, every grazing break a farmer sets, and every alert a vet acts on depends on infrastructure that's reliable, secure, and easy for our engineers to build on. As Halter grows globally and our systems handle billions of daily events from the paddock, the platform underneath needs to scale with us - without slowing anyone down.

We're looking for a Senior Engineer to join our Platform team and help build, run, and evolve the systems that everything else at Halter sits on. You'll bring deep technical expertise to a small team, play a meaningful role in shaping how a fast-growing engineering organisation thinks about cloud infrastructure, developer experience, security, and AI-assisted engineering, and have the autonomy to own significant pieces of the work end-to-end.

Day-to-day you'll work closely with engineering teams across the business - backend, ML, and data - to make sure the platform accelerates their velocity rather than gating it. Whether it's evolving our internal AI tooling into something the whole org relies on, building golden paths that make the right thing the easy thing, hardening our cloud security posture, or keeping our collar-to-cloud pipeline rock-solid as we scale, you'll own problems end-to-end. If you want your work to multiply the impact of every other engineer at Halter, this is the role.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Help shape how Halter leverages AI tooling to accelerate development. We've already invested in internal AI infrastructure that engineers rely on day-to-day, and you'll help it grow from an engineering-team tool into something the whole org leans on - contributing to the adoption patterns, the guardrail to the force-multiplier use cases.

 - Build out the tooling, guardrails, and golden paths that make it easy for other engineers to ship safely and quickly. The right paved roads multiply every engineer's impact, and you'll shape where ours go next.

 - Contribute to the technical direction for our cloud infrastructure as Halter scales globally, helping make the architecture decisions that balance velocity, cost, reliability, and operational simplicity.

 - Bake security into the platform through guardrails and sensible defaults across IAM, network policy, secrets management, and supply chain, so the secure path is also the easy path for every team.

 - Keep our core compute and orchestration layer reliable at the scale farmers and ranchers depend on, day in and day out.

 - Drive observability and incident tooling forward, treating on-call as a signal rather than a cost. Engineers should be able to detect, diagnose, and resolve issues before they reach farmers and ranchers.

 - Automate infrastructure management through Infrastructure-as-Code, CI/CD pipelines, and internal tooling that reduces operational load over time.

 - Contribute to cross-functional architecture discussions and help evolve platform practices and standards, balancing pragmatic delivery with long-term maintainability.

 - Mentor and grow other engineers through design conversations, code reviews, and generous context sharing.

 - Be part of an on-call rotation, working with a highly skilled team to resolve incidents and put preventative measures in place.


YOU'LL BE GREAT IF YOU:

 - Have deep experience building and operating AWS at scale, with strong fluency in container orchestration, cloud networking, and Infrastructure-as-Code. Terraform at scale is a big plus.

 - Have shipped meaningful platform or infrastructure work in a production environment, ideally in a high-growth setting.

 - Understand what good developer experience looks like, and have built golden paths, paved roads, or internal platforms that engineers reach for instead of rolling their own.

 - Treat security as a first-class part of platform engineering, not an afterthought, and have hands-on experience hardening cloud environments.

 - Are excited about how AI tooling can change the way engineering teams work, and have a point of view on where it adds leverage versus where it adds risk.

We’re changing the way the world farms - and with that comes a responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. Halter collars aren’t serviced, aren’t repairable and need to last 6-10 years, anywhere across the globe. The only way we know they will is by testing them relentlessly - and that testing happens in our lab.

As a Test Lab Technician, you’ll be the hands that keep our test lab running. You’ll set up and run tests, move collars between test rigs, put hardware through our production and verification jigs, and keep our equipment maintained, commissioned and calibrated. You’ll also build and modify the test equipment our engineers need, and take ownership of how the lab itself is organised - putting systems in place and holding the standard so that anyone can walk in and find what they need.

This is a hands-on, high-volume, detail-driven role. We’re looking for someone who wants to be genuinely excellent at running test lab operations.  - Set up, run and monitor hardware tests to the documented test plans

 - Move, install and reconfigure collars across test setups

 - Put collars through our production and verification test jigs.

 - Own the day-to-day maintenance of lab equipment - routine servicing, calibration checks, consumables, and getting faulty equipment back into service quickly.

 - Move, install and commission new equipment into the lab, working with suppliers and internal teams to get it up and running and safe to use.

 - Assemble and modify test equipment, fixtures and jigs, including support for delivering on the test equipment builds committed for Q3.

 - Implement and maintain the organisation systems the lab needs - labelling, storage, sample and unit tracking, consumable stock levels.

 - Keep clear records of what was tested, when, on what equipment and with what result, so investigations and reports can rely on the traceability.

 - Communicate proactively with the Hardware Test team on test status, blockers, equipment issues and timelines

 - Follow and improve lab safety and housekeeping practices, raising hazards and near-misses as you see them.

 - Other duties as required from time to time.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Hands-on experience in a lab, workshop, production or field service environment - an electronics, mechatronics or engineering background.

 - Practical hands-on skills: comfortable with hand and power tools, mechanical assembly, basic soldering and wiring, and using test equipment such as multimeters and power supplies.

 - Genuine care for accuracy and process discipline - you follow the test procedure as written, record data properly, and speak up when something doesn’t look right rather than letting it through.

 - A natural organiser. You notice when things are out of place, and you’re motivated by building systems that keep them in place, not just tidying up once.

 - Strong sense of ownership and a bias for action - you see what needs doing and get on with it without waiting to be asked.

 - Clear, honest communication, and comfort working alongside engineers and asking questions when something isn’t clear.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a rare opportunity to be one of Halter's first Regional Sales Managers (Oeste Arenoso), Argentina — one of the world's great cattle nations — building our customer presence in the region from the ground up.

We're looking for a go-getter who is out in the field, meeting farmers, championing Halter and converting them into our very first local customers. A 'never give up attitude' is crucial for this role; as our first sales hire on the ground, you will be a foundational contributor to the growth and success of Halter in Argentina.

You'll be responsible for using your strong sales background to drive end-to-end sales, from cold calling and on-farm meetings to deeply understanding our customers' farm systems. You'll detail Halter's value proposition, progress the sale, and ultimately close the deal. As the region scales, you'll help shape how we set quotas and commissions, build sales capability, and mentor the team that follows you. Make your mark with Halter and help us push the boundaries of farming, connecting animals and humans like never before.



WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Sourcing new leads and opportunities through proactive outreach, referrals/introductions, industry events and other channels, as well as fielding and responding to inbound inquiries.

 - Meeting high growth sales targets by managing pipeline through to close, including screening, qualifying, executing on-farm demonstrations and successfully negotiating contracts with customers.

 - Laying the groundwork for the local sales function — helping to set and manage quotas, commissions and other sales management tasks as the team grows.

 - Coaching, mentoring and developing future sales staff to help drive their professional growth and reach targets as we scale the region.

 - Collaborating with Customer Success to ensure successful post-sales handoff, implementations, customer satisfaction and account renewal.

 - Providing support, insight and communication to help build and foster trusting and enduring relationships with customers as they wait for deployment.

 - Leveraging opportunities and participating in relevant industry/Halter events and demonstrations.

 - Building and leveraging industry relationships to establish and maintain Halter's brand in a brand-new market.

 - Focusing on the customer and their needs, providing feedback to help drive the product roadmap.

 - Working with the team to optimise and evolve the sales process to become faster, more efficient and more predictable as the company scales.
   


WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR 

 - A complete end-to-end sales skill set with at least five years of experience.

 - Proven track records and examples of successfully sourcing new prospects, securing meetings with new leads and creating new sales opportunities.

 - Someone highly experienced in value-based sales with a proven history of closing deals and high-volume sales results.

 - Well-prepared with solid communication skills to present Halter's value proposition.

 - Experience in beef farming or within the agricultural sector is highly desirable.

 - A person who is results-driven, highly motivated with exceptional time management skills.

 - Adaptability in a high-stakes sales environment and the ability to think on your feet — comfort with the ambiguity of building in a new market is a big plus.

 - Sales experience in the technology-based industry is preferred.

 - Fluency in Spanish, with professional working English to collaborate across our global team.

 - A university degree or equivalent would be excellent but not a must.

Argentina is one of the largest beef producers and exporters in the world, with a deep grazing tradition across the Pampas and beyond. This is a founding role as Halter establishes itself in the region — meaning enormous scope to shape how an entire industry adopts virtual fencing technology. You'll be building from the ground up: our first customers, our first relationships, and the foundation of our local team. These opportunities don't come around often.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

Five hundred cattle stand up and walk calmly to their next grazing area. No fences, no dogs, no quad bikes. People say it looks like magic. It is actually solar-powered collars, satellite and mesh connectivity, and machine learning that knows when a cow has eaten enough, how much pasture is left, whether she is healthy, and even who her friends are. Most of this technology did not exist five years ago. We invented it, and we are not slowing down.

You won’t be billing your life in six-minute increments, polishing other people's ideas. At Halter you sit inside a world-class engineering team that ships novel radio protocols, bespoke electronics, firmware, and machine learning at a rapid pace, and we are filing aggressively to hold our global lead. Your job is to find the inventions, sometimes before the engineers realise they have made one, and lock them in.

You will be the second member of our IP team, which means you get to shape how this is done. You’ll bring the patentability analysis, drafting, and prosecution firepower, and you will build the scalable, AI-enhanced systems a rapidly expanding portfolio needs. Expect to spend real time with engineers, reading design docs and code, asking questions until you actually understand how it works, and turning what you find into claims that hold up.

We are adding 500 roles in the next year. That is a constant firehose of new ideas and products.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE:

 - Partner with engineering teams to identify patentable, commercially valuable inventions and draft specifications and claims across firmware, software, machine learning, electronics and mechanical systems.

 - Manage patent prosecution end to end, including examination responses, amendments and strategy, with support from external counsel.

 - Lead freedom-to-operate clearances, working closely with the engineers building the technology.

 - Develop AI-enhanced tools across the IP function. We already use AI heavily and want someone excited to take this further.

 - Join hackathons, uncover patent whitespace, spend time on-farm—and never fill in a timesheet.




YOU'LL CRUSH THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have circa 5-10 years’ experience as Patent Attorney or Patent Engineer.

 - Bring strong technical expertise, or serious interest, across software, electronics or machine learning. We’ll teach you the cow part.

 - Have a real curiosity about how things work. You will dive into design documents and code to find inventions before they are even written down, and keep asking engineers questions until you actually understand it.

 - Have solid experience in patentability assessments, drafting, and prosecution, plus freedom to operate and invalidity work.

 - Have the itch to automate. You see a manual process and you want to kill it.

 - Are comfortable working self-directed. You figure out what needs doing and do it.




BONUS POINTS IF YOU HAVE:

 - A background or real interest in agriculture and agricultural technology.

 - A legal background or litigation experience.

 - An appetite to get stuck into anything you think might matter to Halter, whether or not it says IP on it.




OUR BENEFITS:

 - Delicious snacks and drinks are available for your daily flow.

 - Healthy body, healthy mind. We're partnered with Southern Cross Health Insurance to support your well-being.

 - We offer 6 months of fully paid parental leave for primary caregivers, 4 weeks of fully paid secondary caregiver leave and many other parental benefits that support you and your family.

 - Our personal growth is important. Halter offers an annual $1000 self-development budget to be used for anything that fuels personal growth.

 - Our time to recharge is valued, we're offered wellness leave and unlimited paid annual leave.

 - Importantly, we offer an inclusive and attractive remuneration package made up of salary, benefits and an employee stock ownership plan.




OUR OFFICE FIRST APPROACH:

Humans are wired for connection. Being office first is a core pillar of our culture because in-person connections drive your growth, learning, impact, and relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful work together.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Halter is a dynamic fast paced workplace where our Guidance team is working on Halter’s market leading virtual fencing technology. We are transforming the agriculture industry globally, and you can be a part of that!



We are looking for a Research & Development Specialist to join the team that is continuously developing our virtual fencing product. Everything you need to know to nail this role you’ll learn on the job and you’ll have to work hard to keep up. In this role you’ll be supported to become an expert in virtual fencing. This role is primarily based in the Waikato on our R&D farm close to Morrinsville, where we’ve built our own office in an old calf barn, but you’ll also spend plenty of time in our HQ in Auckland.

What does a Research & Development Specialist do?

As you’ll start to become familiar with the basics of our product, you’ll be supporting and running small projects. We’ll teach you how to use our internal tools to analyse all the data our collars generate and you’ll be testing and validating new versions of our software on our R&D farm.



As your understanding of our product increases you’ll be working closely with our engineers to design and develop new features and functionalities. Most of our R&D starts with some crazy idea that we work out on a whiteboard. You’ll be testing and validating the first prototype and will be supporting the implementation into the product.

Once you know all the intricacies of our system you’ll be independently running trials, visiting Halter farms when they require on-the-ground support and could play a role in our international expansion if you’re up for it.



What we’re looking for

For this role we value hunger over experience! Whether you have loads, little or no experience in Research and Development, we want to hear from you! We’re looking for someone that is incredibly motivated, loves solving hard problems and has an incredible attitude. You can’t be afraid to get your hands dirty though, because about half of your work will be outdoors on our farm. Cattle are amazing and intelligent animals to work with and you should be as least as excited about working with them as we are.

If you love the unknown, are hungry for adventure and have a strong desire to learn new things, then this might be the right role for you. It’s important to you that your work matters and you want to have an impact on people, animals and a global industry.

At Halter we value getting shit done and this isn’t a 9-5 job. We didn’t become one of NZ's fastest growing companies by fluffing around. We’re looking for someone that is looking for a challenge and is eager to go above and beyond to help Halter achieve our mission.

We’re looking for someone that has insane critical thinking abilities, is able to thoroughly analyse problems and can come up with innovative and creative solutions to hard problems, even when they may seem unsolvable. You thrive in ambiguity and use your initiative when needed. You’re not afraid to ask questions, to share your opinion and to think out of the box. And of course; we’re looking for someone that can have some fun in the workplace.

 - Manage collar stock on customer farms, making sure levels are accurate and nothing slips through the cracks

 - Pack and dispatch urgent spare collars to farms that need them fast

 - Ship collars back to AKL HQ and keep logistics running smoothly

 - Conduct hardware audits and trials on customer farms.

 - Be a positive, professional face of Halter when you're on-farm with our customers



WHAT YOU WILL BRING

 - Physically fit and up for the manual side of the work

 - Reliable, punctual, and someone who takes ownership, if you say you'll be there, you're there

 - A strong work ethic with a track record to back it up

 - Comfortable working independently on the road and as part of a team when back at base

At Halter, we're on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations in the world. Our customers use Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional farming. Imagine 500 cattle standing up and walking calmly to their next break. No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences, just a herd moving at its own pace. People say it looks like magic. Underneath it is a fleet of tens of 1 million (and growing rapidly) collars, each one a small physical system balancing power, radios, sensors and firmware, all operating on a live animal, in the real world, at scale.

We're looking for a Device Systems Engineer to help guide the development of our devices to extract the absolute best performance for our customers. This is a role for someone who wants to build a genuinely deep understanding of the product in the wild: where power gets spent, where the physical world doesn't match the assumptions in the design, and where there's real headroom to do better. You'll spend your time in the data, but the point isn't the data itself. It's the insight it gives you into a physical system, and the improvements you can drive because of it.

This role sits at the intersection of firmware, hardware, comms and data. You'll need to be equally comfortable wrangling a massive, noisy, real-world dataset and reasoning from first principles about what a sensor or a radio can and can't actually do. And critically, you won't just hand off a finding. You'll see it through: forming the hypothesis, proving it in data, working out what to change, and following it into production.

Our team out-thinks, out-works and out-cares. We're committed to delivering real change in the world. This isn't easy, and honestly, we love that it's hard.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Analyse collar performance at fleet scale: power consumption, battery life, GPS and sensor behaviour, across tens of millions of devices operating in wildly different real-world conditions.

 - Build a deep, ground-truth understanding of how the product is actually used on farm, and how that differs from how we assumed it would be used when we designed it.

 - Wrangle large, messy, real-world datasets (fleet telemetry, logs, field data) to find the signal in the noise, and know the difference between a genuine effect and a data quality artefact.

 - Reason from first principles about the physical limitations of sensors, radios and batteries, so you can tell when a performance gap is a physics problem, a firmware problem, or a usage pattern problem.

 - Bring your ground-truth understanding of real-world device performance into the scoping and design of new products and hardware revisions. Your view of what actually happens in the field, not just what happens on the bench, will be critical to the whole team arriving at the best possible product.

 - Communicate findings clearly to firmware, hardware and product teams, translating deep technical analysis into something people can actually act on and prioritise.

 - See improvements through from insight to production: working with engineering teams to implement, validate and confirm the change actually delivered what the data said it would.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Deep curiosity about how things actually work, and the patience to dig until you genuinely understand it.

 - Genuine first-principles thinking. You default to reasoning about a system from how it actually works physically, rather than pattern-matching to what usually works.

 - A bias to ownership and follow-through. You're not satisfied with an interesting finding; you want to see it become a real improvement in the fleet.

 - An engineering science, physics, or similarly quantitative technical background, with a track record of applying it to real, messy, physical-world problems.

ABOUT THE ROLE
